text:
The fault is most likely in the bias mirror. Power is 2.5× over budget (999 µW against 400 µW) while gain, bandwidth and offset all pass. That pattern means one branch is drawing too much current, not that the amplifier is mis-sized. I worked this out by hand from the netlist; I did not run any simulation.

**Current budget.** M6 (W = 0.49) is the diode that sets the reference. M5 (W = 2.02) mirrors it about 4.1× into the input-pair tail. M8 (W = 7.5, m = 3, so 22.5 µm effective) mirrors it about 46× into the output stage. All three have L = 2.34. Total current is roughly I_bias × (1 + 4.1 + 46), about 51 × I_bias. The measured 999 µW is about 555 µA, which gives I_bias ≈ 11 µA. The output stage alone carries about 500 µA.

**If M8 were m = 1.** The output branch drops to about 15× I_bias. Total power falls to about 400 µW, right at the limit. The closed-loop behaviour would barely change, because the loop sets the gain, and the bandwidth still has margin. That fits a single multiplier fault on M8 very well.

**Alternative.** If M6 had been shrunk instead, every mirror ratio would grow together and give the same symptom. For example, with M6 at about 1.47 µm, power would be roughly 320 µW. So M6 is the second candidate, and M5 is a distant third. The tail current adds comparatively little to the total.

{"ranking": ["M8", "M6", "M5"], "fault": "Output-stage current-sink M8 oversized (m=3 instead of 1, ~3x too much mirror ratio from ibias), so the output branch draws ~500 uA and total power is ~1 mW"}
